                                              \label{eq:v81-eigen-local}
\end{align}
The constants are independent of the two widths and the length $d$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The interpolation proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:v80-interpolation} applies
with the stricter refinement \eqref{eq:v81-peak-refinement} and
exponent $\theta$. In the short-power case use
$|\ell(P_bQ^dh)|\le C|Q^dh|_w\le C(1+d)|h|_w$;
in the long-power case apply the strong inequality at the balancing
time and use power boundedness afterwards. The factor $1+|\log t|$
is absorbed between the exponents $255/256$ and $31/32$.

For completeness we specify the physical vector used to localize
$v_\xi$. At a unit-modulus point the inherited physical peripheral
 theorem, Supplement Theorem~\ref{supp-thm:v40-full-peripheral}, gives
a strong-space eigenvector $u_*$ with $|u_*|=1$ almost everywhere.
Choose a weakly continuous smooth test whose pairing with $u_*$ is
nonzero. Weak continuity of the continued projection makes
$\Pi_\xi u_*$ nonzero on a smaller chart, with that pairing bounded
away from zero. Normalize by this pairing. A finite cover supplies
common constants. The invariant coordinate cylinder is the same
for the circular family, so $u_*$ remains a physical bounded function
when used at neighboring parameters. For all real frequencies,
$|Q^Lu_*|=1$ in the physical realization.
The weak estimates are justified by bounded strong approximants,
not by assigning arbitrary stable-curve traces to an $L^\infty$
representative. The physical Cesaro construction in the cited
peripheral theorem realizes $u_*$ as a strong limit of uniformly
bounded finite Cesaro sums of powers at the reference parameter
applied to one fixed smooth bounded vector, followed by a fixed
normalization. At neighboring real parameters, applying a fixed
power $Q^L$ to these finite physical sums preserves their uniform
modulus bound. Endpoint and homogeneous-incidence intersections
therefore satisfy the same length bounds on every approximant.
Boundedness of the fixed power and multipliers on the common strong
space permits passage to the weak limit. Only after that passage
is the integer $L$ chosen below. Thus the length estimates do not
require a trace assertion for arbitrary bounded measurable densities.

Use
\[
 \Pi_\xi u_*=\lambda^{-L}Q^Lu_*-\lambda^{-L}N^Lu_*.
\]
For $P_b$ choose $L=\lceil\log(1/b)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil$.
The weak norm is at most $Cr_*^{-L}(b+b^{1/8}\rho^L)$,
which is bounded by $Cb^{63/64}$ under
\eqref{eq:v81-peak-refinement}. For $M_s$ choose instead
$L=\lceil(3/2)\log(1/s)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil$.
The homogeneous length estimate, valid for every physical vector
of modulus at most one, gives
$Cr_*^{-L}(s^{3/2}+s^{1/8}\rho^L)\le Cs^{47/32}$.
The bounded strong multiplier gives the last assertion. This
argument neither assigns physical modulus one to a continued
nonperipheral eigenvector nor divides by $\Pi\one$.
\end{proof}

Set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-exponents}
              \alpha=\frac{129}{128},\qquad
              \beta=\frac{17}{16},\qquad
              \delta=\alpha-1=\frac1{128}.
\end{equation}
Let $D_b=\{|p_0|<b,\ |p_m|<b\}$. In the next theorem the endpoint
marks are retained even when the initial and terminal section tests
are dropped in a positive upper comparison.

\begin{theorem}[Two-endpoint, one-incidence local bound]
\label{thm:v81-joint-local}
For every fixed auxiliary band $B_*$ there are $C_{B_*}<\infty$ and
$\rho_{B_*}<1$ such that, uniformly in $R,m\ge2$, $0\le j\le m$,
exact labels, intervals $J$, and $0<b<b_0$, $0<s<s_0$,
\begin{align}
 &m^2\nu\{K_m^{\rm c}=k,A_m=l,L_m\in J,\ D_b,\ c_j<s\}
                                                        \notag\\
 &\quad\le Cb^\alpha s^\beta(|J|+B_*^{-1})
   +C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2
                   \min\{b\rho_{B_*}^{m/2},s^2\}.
                                      \label{eq:v81-joint-local}
\end{align}
The leading constant is independent of the previously fixed band.
The estimate is on the original occupation coefficient, not on a
reversed or neighboring occupation class.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The characteristic pairing is exactly
\[
             \ell(P_bQ^{m-j}M_sQ^jP_b\one).
\]
Suppose first $m-j\ge m/2$. Put $h=M_sQ^jP_b\one$.
Power boundedness and \eqref{eq:v81-small-vector} give
$\|h\|\le Cb^{7/8}$. Its physical realization has modulus at most
one, so $|h|_w\le Cs^{3/2}$. The long-block leading term has
amplitude at most
\[
 Cb^{63/64+(7/8)(1/32)}s^{(3/2)(31/32)}
                  =Cb^{259/256}s^{93/64}.
\]
Its remainder is bounded by $Cb\rho^{m/2}$, using the terminal
factor $b^{1/8}$ as well as the initial strong factor $b^{7/8}$.

If $j\ge m/2$, expand $Q^jP_b\one$ instead. Its projected
coefficient is at most $Cb^{255/256}$ by
\eqref{eq:v81-interpolation}. Set $h=M_sv_\xi$ and $d=m-j$.
There are two bounds for the remaining terminal pairing:
\[
 |\ell(P_bQ^dh)|\le Cb^{1/8},\qquad
 |\ell(P_bQ^dh)|\le Cs^{1457/1024}.
\]
The first uses strong power boundedness and
\eqref{eq:v81-terminal-small}; the second uses
\eqref{eq:v81-interpolation} and \eqref{eq:v81-eigen-local}.
Their geometric interpolation with powers $1/4$ and $3/4$ gives
$Cb^{1/32}s^{4371/4096}$. Thus the leading amplitude in this
case is at most $Cb^{263/256}s^{4371/4096}$.
The remainder is again $Cb\rho^{m/2}$. Both leading bounds imply
$Cb^\alpha s^\beta$, since
$259/256>129/128$ and $4371/4096>17/16$.

The long spectral factor in either case has a four-frequency
Gaussian integral of order $m^{-2}$. On the fixed-band complement
the long block has an exponential gap and the same endpoint norm
factors. Independently, the physical characteristic pairing is at
most $\nu(c_j<s)\le s^2$ at every real frequency. Applying
$|z|\le A+D$, $|z|\le V\Rightarrow |z|\le A+\min(D,V)$
retains the cap in \eqref{eq:v81-joint-local}. The positive interval
majorant and exact torus coefficient extraction now give that
estimate. No number of physical words occurs in the argument.
\end{proof}

\section{Mixed critical volume insertions}
\label{sec:v81-mixed}
The joint estimate has a critical-width gain greater than one.
It supplies a uniform estimate for the first inverse gradient with
a fixed positive truncation, and actual untruncated fractional
inverse-gradient insertions. The distinction is visible in the
finite-count remainder and will be retained in the roof-height argument.

Keep the original additive insertion $I_m$ of
\eqref{eq:v80-depth-insertion}. Write $z=|g|$ on the regular exact
event and, for a small fixed $b>0$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-critical-volume}
 u^b(t)\,dt=L_\#(I_m\one_{\{z<b\}}\one_\Pi\nu_R^*).
\end{equation}
The threshold $b$ now measures $|g|$, not the momentum coordinate.
Since $\{z<b\}\subset D_{b/R_-}$, the difference changes only
uniform constants. There is a fixed $b_1>0$ for which the following
statements hold for $b<b_1$.

\begin{theorem}[Critical localization of the complete optical source]
\label{thm:v81-critical-volume}
For every fixed band $B_*$,
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_Ju^b(t)\,dt
 \le{}&Cb^\alpha(|J|+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2 b^{1/2}\rho_{B_*}^{m/4}.
                                      \label{eq:v81-critical-finite}
\end{align}
Consequently, for every previously fixed roof width $r>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-critical-average}
       \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2\|A_ru^b\|_\infty\le Cb^\alpha.
\end{equation}
Every inverse-incidence scale and every actual word is included
before the collision limit.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Insert the positive layer cake for
$c_j^{-1}\one_{\{c_j<s_0\}}$ into
\eqref{eq:v81-joint-local}. Its leading integral is finite because
$\beta>1$. In the capped remainder put $D=b\rho_{B_*}^{m/2}$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:v80-cap-integral}, with exponent one, bounds the
entire remainder by $C\sqrt D$; the cap is integrated before the
collision limit. This gives the stated $b^{1/2}$ error.

For the bounded complementary part of $c_j^{-1}$ and the constant
one, the endpoint-only pairing is $\ell(P_bQ^mP_b\one)$.
Its leading amplitude is at most
$Cb^{7/8+63/64}$, and its remainder is at most
$Cb\rho^m$. These are bounded by the respective terms in
\eqref{eq:v81-critical-finite}. Sum the internal marks with
weights $q_0^{d_j}$, whose sum is uniformly bounded. Dropping only
the section tests in each positive comparison retains $D_{b/R_-}$,
the mark and the same exact $(k,n,m)$ coefficient, with the sole
normalization factor $c_*^{-1}$. It does not alter the defined source.
Finally divide by $2r$, take the collision limit with $B_*$ fixed,
and enlarge that band afterwards. This proves
\eqref{eq:v81-critical-average}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual fractional and truncated first inverse gradients]
\label{thm:v81-gradient-insertions}
For $0<\eta<1/2$, the actual measure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-fractional-source}
 v^{\eta,b}(t)\,dt
   =L_\#(I_m z^{-\eta}\one_{\{0<z<b\}}\one_\Pi\nu_R^*)
\end{equation}
is finite at each count and satisfies
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_Jv^{\eta,b}(t)\,dt
 \le{}&C_\eta b^{\alpha-\eta}(|J|+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C_{B_*,\eta}(1+B_*|J|)m^2
                 b^{1/2-\eta}\rho_{B_*}^{m/4}.
                                      \label{eq:v81-fractional-finite}
\end{align}
In particular its fixed-width collision-normalized height is at
most $C_\eta b^{\alpha-\eta}$.

For $0<a<b<b_1$, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-truncated-source}
 v^{a,b}(t)\,dt
   =L_\#(I_m z^{-1}\one_{\{a\le z<b\}}\one_\Pi\nu_R^*).
\end{equation}
This source obeys
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_Jv^{a,b}(t)\,dt
 \le{}&Cb^\delta(|J|+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2 a^{-1/2}\rho_{B_*}^{m/4}.
                                      \label{eq:v81-truncated-finite}
\end{align}
Thus, for each fixed $a,b,r>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-truncated-average}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2\|A_rv^{a,b}\|_\infty\le Cb^\delta,
 \qquad \delta=1/128,
\end{equation}
with a leading constant independent of the lower truncation $a$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For the fractional assertion use
\[
 z^{-\eta}\one_{\{z<b\}}
   =b^{-\eta}\one_{\{z<b\}}
       +\eta\int_0^b q^{-\eta-1}\one_{\{z<q\}}\,dq
\]
on $z>0$. Apply \eqref{eq:v81-critical-finite} first with a positive
lower integration limit, and then use monotone convergence. Both
integrals are finite: their exponents are $\alpha-\eta>0$ and
$1/2-\eta>0$. This proves physical finiteness as well as
\eqref{eq:v81-fractional-finite}, not just convergence of a
formal leading term. The removed set $g=0$ has zero source area;
no value assigned there affects the measure.

For the first inverse power a convenient positive majorant is
\[
 z^{-1}\one_{\{a\le z<b\}}
 \le b^{-1}\one_{\{z<b\}}+
                    \int_a^b q^{-2}\one_{\{z<q\}}\,dq.
\]
The leading term in \eqref{eq:v81-critical-finite} gives
$C\{b^{\alpha-1}+\int_a^b q^{\alpha-2}\,dq\}\le Cb^\delta$.
The error gives
$C\{b^{-1/2}+\int_a^b q^{-3/2}\,dq\}\le Ca^{-1/2}$.
This proves \eqref{eq:v81-truncated-finite}. The ordered fixed-width
limits prove the remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

Let $v^a$ be the same exact source with insertion
$I_m z^{-1}\one_{\{z\ge a\}}$. Split it at $b_1/2$, and use
\eqref{eq:v80-depth-source} on the part above that threshold.
For every fixed $a,r>0$ this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v81-full-truncation}
             \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2\|A_rv^a\|_\infty\le C,
\end{equation}
where $C$ is independent of $a$. This statement does not assert the
same conclusion for the untruncated first inverse gradient. The
factor $a^{-1/2}$ in \eqref{eq:v81-truncated-finite} prevents taking
$a\downarrow0$ before the collision limit by this proof. By contrast,
\eqref{eq:v81-fractional-finite} is an actual untruncated insertion
throughout the stated range $\eta<1/2$.

\section{Measurable maximal segments and cutoff-uniform source bounds}
\label{sec:v85-segments}
All surfaces in this article are counted with their incident physical
component. The following parametrization makes this convention, and the
absence of a word-count factor, explicit. Fix $m,R,n,k$ throughout its
construction. Let $\Omega$ be the regular exact event, with the critical
points of $F$ removed, and let $\tau^\pm$ be the two lifetimes of $X$.
Write $\bar\nu=\nu_R^*|_\Omega$.

\begin{theorem}[A Borel parametrization of maximal regular segments]
\label{thm:v85-segment-map}
There are countably many Borel sets $E_j$ in lifted angular intervals,
Borel functions $a_j<b_j$, and a Borel bijection
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v85-segment-map}
 \Psi:\coprod_j\{(\theta,u):\theta\in E_j,\ a_j(\theta)<u<b_j(\theta)\}
                  \longrightarrow\Omega
\end{equation}
with Borel inverse, such that each $\theta\in E_j$ labels one entire
maximal segment, $F(\Psi_j(\theta,u))=u$, and
$\vartheta(\Psi_j(\theta,u))=\theta$ modulo $2\pi$. Its physical
angular density is
\[
 A_j(u,\theta)=\frac{\omega(\Psi_j(\theta,u))}
                         {4\pi c_*\chi(\Psi_j(\theta,u))}.
\]
For every nonnegative Borel function $f$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v85-segment-area}
 \int_\Omega f\,d\bar\nu
   =\sum_j\int_{E_j}\int_{a_j(\theta)}^{b_j(\theta)}
           f(\Psi_j(\theta,u))A_j(u,\theta)\,du\,d\theta.
\end{equation}
The same identity holds with any Borel selector of the segment and its
interior point. For almost every $t$, disintegration gives the
corresponding identity on $\mu_t$, with $u=t$. Both identities are
identities of measures, not estimates with an unspecified multiplicity.

Restrict to segments with a nongrazing forward endpoint. The endpoint
map, retaining the incident one-sided component, is Borel and injective
outside the transverse null sets of the first-exit construction. Its
outgoing measure in these coordinates is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v85-segment-face}
                    d\zeta_+=A_j(b_j-,\theta)\,d\theta.
\end{equation}
Each such face and an intermediate roof determine at most one physical
interior state. In particular, summing a variation integral over these
segments gives exactly the selected physical volume integral in
\eqref{eq:v85-segment-area}.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Enumerate the rational numbers as $q_1,q_2,\ldots$. The lifetime
functions of a smooth flow on an open set are lower semicontinuous;
this also follows by covering each compact surviving segment with
finitely many ordinary flow boxes. They are therefore Borel. Since
$XF=1$ and $F$ is bounded at fixed count, the roof interval of every
maximal segment is a bounded, nonempty open interval.

On the smooth transverse slice $\Sigma_i=\Omega\cap\{F=q_i\}$,
keep the points whose maximal interval contains none of
$q_1,\ldots,q_{i-1}$. These are Borel conditions on the lifetimes.
Every maximal segment has exactly one representative in this union:
use the first rational in its roof interval and strict monotonicity of
$F$. On each slice, $\vartheta$ is a local coordinate, since
$\det D_q(F,\vartheta)=\chi>0$. Cover the slices by countably many
angular charts, and disjointize their representatives by the first
containing chart. Denote the resulting Borel angular subsets by $E_j$,
and the associated representative by $\xi_j(\theta)$, at roof $q_{i(j)}$.
Put
\[
 a_j=q_{i(j)}-\tau^-(\xi_j),\qquad
 b_j=q_{i(j)}+\tau^+(\xi_j),\qquad
 \Psi_j(\theta,u)=\Phi_{u-q_{i(j)}}\xi_j(\theta).
\]
The flow is continuous on its open lifetime domain. This proves Borel
measurability. The inverse is explicit: for $x$, select the first
rational in its maximal roof interval, flow to that roof, and select
the first angular chart containing the representative. All these
selections are Borel. If two parameter points have the same image,
uniqueness of the flow gives the same maximal segment and representative;
then $F=u$ and the angular chart give identical parameters. This proves
\eqref{eq:v85-segment-map} without a quotient measurability assumption.
The Borel seams assign representatives only; they are not new exits.

In a local angular flow box, change of variables from endpoint angles
has density $\omega/(4\pi c_*\chi)$. The same formula at another roof
follows by physical coarea covariance; the transverse angle is unchanged.
Apply this local formula on countably many Borel-disjoint restrictions
of the parametrization and use Tonelli. It gives
\eqref{eq:v85-segment-area} for every Borel selector. Disintegration over
$u$ and a countable determining algebra give equality of fiber measures
outside one null set in $t$, then equality for all nonnegative Borel
functions. Additional external variables use the product graph and
Fubini, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:v83-common-kernel}.

The endpoint limits exist by the all-contact motion estimate. They are
Borel as limits along the interior roofs
$b_j-\min\{1/N,(b_j-a_j)/2\}$. A nongrazing forward endpoint has
positive limiting gradient and a one-sided smooth stationary-word
extension. The flow-box contraction of the physical area form gives
\eqref{eq:v85-segment-face}. Two coincident geometric boundary points
on different incident components are different faces by definition.
On one incident component, uniqueness of the backward regular flow
makes its interior segment unique. Tangent and lower-dimensional
strata have the transverse-null convention of
Proposition~\ref{prop:v83-first-exit-kernel}; removing their flow
saturations removes no area in \eqref{eq:v85-segment-area}. This proves
the last assertions. No continuation past a true physical boundary is
used, and a backward critical endpoint remains an endpoint of its
segment, not a chart seam.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The lower cutoff and its finite-count remainder}
We record the quantitative step behind the cutoff-independent constant
used in boundary transfer. It concerns an actual positive volume source;
it is not a surface insertion theorem. Write $z=|g|$, $\alpha=129/128$,
and
\[
 u^b(t)\,dt=F_\#(I_m\one_{\{z<b\}}\bar\nu),\quad
 v^{c,b}(t)\,dt=F_\#(I_mz^{-1}\one_{\{c\le z<b\}}\bar\nu),\quad
 v^c(t)\,dt=F_\#(I_mz^{-1}\one_{\{z\ge c\}}\bar\nu).
\]
The source-pinned critical-volume estimate, including its remainder, is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v85-critical-input}
 m^2\int_Ju^b\le Cb^\alpha(|J|+B_*^{-1})
 +C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2b^{1/2}\rho_{B_*}^{m/4}.
\end{equation}
It is Supplement equation~\eqref{supp-v81archive:eq:v81-critical-finite}.
Its dependence on the joint spectral theorem is listed in the dependency
map; it is restated here, not independently recertified.

\begin{proposition}[Uniform leading constant at every positive cutoff]
\label{prop:v85-cutoff}
For $0<c<b<b_1$, the complete exact source satisfies
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_Jv^{c,b}
 \le{}&C\left(1+\frac1{\alpha-1}\right)b^{\alpha-1}
                                      (|J|+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+2C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2c^{-1/2}\rho_{B_*}^{m/4}.
                                             \label{eq:v85-cutoff-finite}
\end{align}
Consequently, for every fixed $c,L>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v85-cutoff-uniform}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}\sup_{|J|=L}m^2\int_Jv^c\le C_0 L,
 \qquad C_0\text{ independent of }c\text{ and }L.
\end{equation}
No assertion at $c=0$, or at a collision-dependent $c$, is made.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use the positive majorant
\[
 z^{-1}\one_{\{c\le z<b\}}
 \le b^{-1}\one_{\{z<b\}}+\int_c^b q^{-2}\one_{\{z<q\}}\,dq.
\]
Insert \eqref{eq:v85-critical-input} before any limit. The leading
coefficient is at most
$b^{\alpha-1}+\int_c^b q^{\alpha-2}\,dq
\le(1+(\alpha-1)^{-1})b^{\alpha-1}$.
The error coefficient is
$b^{-1/2}+\int_c^b q^{-3/2}\,dq
=2c^{-1/2}-b^{-1/2}\le2c^{-1/2}$.
This proves \eqref{eq:v85-cutoff-finite}. Split $v^c$ at the fixed
threshold $b_1/2$. Above it, use the complete depth-weighted source
estimate of Supplement Corollary~\ref{supp-v80archive:cor:v80-depth-source}.
Below it, apply \eqref{eq:v85-cutoff-finite}, first fixing $c,L,B_*$,
then taking the collision limsup, and then enlarging $B_*$. If
$c\ge b_1/2$, positivity gives the same conclusion. The surviving
leading constant contains only fixed physical thresholds, not $c$.
The displayed finite-count error explains why removal of $c$ before
the collision limit is a separate question.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The audited paired-transfer estimate]
\label{cor:v85-audited-transfer}
On any Borel subfamily of short segments with $b-a\le2r$ and
$z(b-)^2\ge8\Lambda_\circ r$, let $S_r^+$ and $S_r^-$ use the
same exit-window kernel and the outgoing and incoming angular traces,
respectively. Then
\[
 |S_r^+(t)-S_r^-(t)|\le C\int_{t-2r}^{t+2r}v^{c_r}(u)\,du,
 \qquad c_r=2\sqrt{\Lambda_\circ r},
\]
and their ordered global essential-height difference is at most
$4CC_0r$, with $C_0$ independent of $c_r>0$. A grazing incoming
trace is zero, so its entire outgoing contribution obeys this bound.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Radial growth keeps the full segment above $c_r$. Differentiate the
physical angular density, retaining both factors:
$|\partial_u A|\le C A I_m/z$, as proved in Supplement
Lemma~\ref{supp-v84archive:lem:v84-angular-variation}. At a grazing
incoming end $\omega\to0$ while $\chi\ge\lambda_\circ$; at any
nongrazing end the one-sided regular extension gives its trace.
Integrate the absolute variation between these traces. When its kernel
is nonzero the full selected segment lies in $(t-2r,t+2r)$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:v85-segment-map} identifies the complete sum with a
selected submeasure of $v^{c_r}(u)\,du$, with multiplicity one.
Positive approximation proves the assertion for all selected sheets.
Apply \eqref{eq:v85-cutoff-uniform} with $L=4r$. This supplies the
named map, exact measure, and cutoff uniformity in the same argument.
\end{proof}

\section{Two-sided physical ends and oscillation of the original source}
\label{sec:v90-two-sided}
Fix an exact event, and use its Borel maximal-segment coordinates
$(\sigma,u)$, with $a_\sigma<u<b_\sigma$. The measure $d\sigma$
includes the disjoint angular charts and their incident components.
Write $A_\sigma(u)$ for the physical density, $z=|g|$, and
$\ell_\sigma=b_\sigma-a_\sigma$. In this section
\[
 \gamma=\frac1{32},\qquad \eta=\frac14,\qquad
 \kappa=\frac{1-\eta}{2}=\frac38,\qquad v=v^{1/4}.
\]
Every estimate is on the original collision source. In particular a
backward end is an end of the roof flow in the same exact event, not
a reversal or relabeling of the billiard record.

\begin{lemma}[Both physical end layers]\label{lem:v90-ends}
Let
\[
 e_s^\pm(t)=\int\one_{\{\tau^\pm\le s\}}\,d\mu_t.
\]
Backward critical termination is included in $e_s^-$. There are
$s_0,C>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-end-cap}
 \bar\nu\{\tau^\pm\le s\}\le C\sqrt s\qquad(0<s<s_0).
\end{equation}
For every fixed auxiliary band $B_*$, after increasing its constants
and choosing one $0<\theta_{B_*}<1$, both signs satisfy
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_J e_s^\pm(t)\,dt
 \le{}& Cs^\gamma(|J|+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^3
                        \min\{\theta_{B_*}^{m},\sqrt s\}.
                                             \label{eq:v90-end-finite}
\end{align}
The constants are uniform in all finite $m\ge2$, radii and exact labels.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The forward inclusion is \eqref{eq:v83-layer-input}. For a backward
segment of length at most $s$, apply the same contact-motion estimate
to the segment with its earlier endpoint as the starting point. Its
endpoint-curve length is at most $C\sqrt s$, and each contact and
flight margin changes by at most its prescribed depth weight times
that length. If the limiting backward end is regular and noncritical,
strictly positive incidences, clearances and section-edge distances
would continue both the word and the field, contradicting maximality.
Thus the same three physical layers contain this case. If the limit
is critical, radial growth gives instead
\[
                     z(x)^2\le2\Lambda_\circ s.
\]
These alternatives also cover simultaneous failures. No chart seam
is used as an end.

The physical estimates used in the complete residence cap apply to
each of the three layers: incidence has mass at most $w^2$, a section
strip has mass at most $Cw$, and the image-collision clearance envelope
has mass at most $Cw$. At widths $Cq_0^d\sqrt s$ their complete depth
sum is $O(\sqrt s)$. The additional critical set lies in
$\{|p_0|\le C\sqrt s\}$, of invariant mass $O(\sqrt s)$. Dropping
the section tests on these positive upper comparisons costs exactly
$c_*^{-1}$. This proves \eqref{eq:v90-end-cap} for the original
source, without changing its labels.

For the localized estimate, the incidence and clearance layers are
contained in the original bad source at an auxiliary parameter
$C\sqrt s$. The section layers use \eqref{eq:v83-strip-input},
summed at their depth widths. This is the forward finite-count exit
proof and applies to the same layers on the backward side. For the
critical alternative use the retained endpoint-only bound
\[
 m^2\bar\nu\{F\in J,z<\zeta\}
 \le C\zeta^{129/128}(|J|+B_*^{-1})
       +C_{B_*}(1+B_*|J|)m^2\zeta\rho_{B_*}^{m/2}.
\]
At $\zeta=C\sqrt s$ its leading term is smaller than $Cs^\gamma$.
This proves the uncapped version of \eqref{eq:v90-end-finite}.
Apply $x\le P+D$, $x\le V\Rightarrow x\le P+\min(D,V)$ to
that positive mass and \eqref{eq:v90-end-cap}. Since $m^2\le m^3$,
adjusting constants gives the displayed common cap. It is a cap on
the positive estimate, not a claim that an isolated signed spectral
remainder has the physical bound.
\end{proof}

For use below the complete sources $p$ and $v$ obey the retained
finite-count estimate
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-volume-finite}
 m^2\int_J(p+v)\le U_{m,B_*}(|J|),\quad
 U_{m,B_*}(L)=C(L+B_*^{-1})
                   +C_{B_*}(1+B_*L)m^3\theta_{B_*}^{m}.
\end{equation}
Its constants may be enlarged from those in
\eqref{eq:v90-end-finite}. The stated fractional source, not an
untruncated first inverse gradient, is used here.

\begin{lemma}[A fixed-band envelope at every microscopic scale]
\label{lem:v90-remainder-envelope}
For $0<\theta<1$ and $0<s<1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-cap-log}
 \sup_{m\ge2}m^3\min\{\theta^m,\sqrt s\}
          \le C_\theta\sqrt s(1+|\log s|)^3.
\end{equation}
Consequently, at every one fixed admissible band and fixed $L$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-uniform-end}
 \sup_{m,R,n,k}\sup_{|J|\le L}m^2\int_J e_s^\pm
                \le K_{B_*,L}s^\gamma,\qquad
 \sup_m U_{m,B_*}(L)<\infty.
\end{equation}
These suprema precede $s\downarrow0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Put $a=-\log\theta$ and $M_s=\max\{2,a^{-1}\log(s^{-1/2})\}$.
For $m\le M_s$, use $m^3\sqrt s$. For $m>M_s$, write
$m=M_s+y$ and use
$(M_s+y)^3e^{-ay}\le C_a(1+M_s)^3$; when $M_s=2$ the
same estimate follows after increasing $C_a$. This proves
\eqref{eq:v90-cap-log}. Since $\gamma<1/2$,
$s^{1/2-\gamma}(1+|\log s|)^3$ is bounded on $(0,1)$.
Substitution in \eqref{eq:v90-end-finite} proves the first assertion
of \eqref{eq:v90-uniform-end}. Exponential decay proves the second.
No Fourier band is allowed to grow with the collision count.
\end{proof}

Extend
\[
 f_\sigma^\varepsilon(u)=A_\sigma(u)W^\varepsilon(\Psi_\sigma(u))
\]
by zero outside $(a_\sigma,b_\sigma)$. Define the lifted oscillation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-lifted-oscillation}
 \Xi_h^\varepsilon(J)=\int_J\int
    |f_\sigma^\varepsilon(t+h)-f_\sigma^\varepsilon(t)|\,d\sigma\,dt.
\end{equation}
This keeps the absolute value before the complete physical sum.
It therefore dominates $\int_J|b^\varepsilon(t+h)-b^\varepsilon(t)|dt$.

\begin{theorem}[All-scale oscillation of the original weighted source]
\label{thm:v90-whole-oscillation}
For each fixed $L$ and one fixed admissible band there is $K_{B_*,L}$
such that, for every $m\ge2$, every exact event, every $0<h<h_0$ and
$0<\varepsilon\le1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-whole-oscillation}
 m^2\Xi_h^\varepsilon(J)
       \le K_{B_*,L}\bigl(h^{1/32}+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt h\bigr)
                         \qquad(|J|\le L).
\end{equation}
The estimate includes every true forward end, backward end and
critical entrance. It is not restricted to common survivors.
For $p$, the unweighted version has no guard-derivative term.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The all-contact first derivatives and the product rule for factors in
$[0,1]$ give
\[
 |D_qW^\varepsilon|\le
 C\varepsilon^{-1}\sum_{d\ge0}q_0^{3d/4}
 \le C_\Theta\varepsilon^{-1}.
\]
This uses the original smooth guard and requires no monotonicity of
$\Theta$. Since $|X_q|\le C/z$, its derivative on each regular
segment satisfies $|(W^\varepsilon)'|\le C_\Theta\varepsilon^{-1}/z$
almost everywhere. Together with the full angular-density derivative,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v90-weighted-derivative}
 |(f_\sigma^\varepsilon)'|
       \le C A_\sigma I_m/z+C_\Theta\varepsilon^{-1}A_\sigma/z.
\end{equation}
Local absolute continuity suffices; all subsequent integrals are
first taken on compact subsegments.

For a pair $t,t+h$ on the same segment, integrate
\eqref{eq:v90-weighted-derivative}. In the subsequent integral over
$t\in J$, an intermediate roof $u$ is counted for a set of starting
roofs of length at most $\min\{h,u-a_\sigma\}$. Radial growth from
the lower endpoint gives $z(u)^2\ge2\lambda_\circ(u-a_\sigma)$.
Thus
\begin{align*}
 \frac{\min(h,u-a_\sigma)}{z(u)}
     &\le C h^{5/8}z(u)^{-1/4},\\
 \frac{\min(h,u-a_\sigma)}{z(u)}&\le C\sqrt h.
\end{align*}
Use the first inequality for optical variation and the second for
the guard. By the Borel bijection their complete sums are bounded by
\[
 C h^{5/8}\int_{J+(0,h)}v(u)\,du
        +C_\Theta\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt h\int_{J+(0,h)}p(u)\,du.
\]
There is no physical-word multiplicity. Tonelli and positive
exhaustion justify the sum even when the unweighted derivative
$A_\sigma I_m/z$ is not globally integrable.

If only $t$ is on a segment, its contribution is at most $e_h^+(t)$.
If only $t+h$ is on it, its contribution is at most $e_h^-(t+h)$.
These are the actual original end layers. Therefore the preceding
drift bound plus $\int_Je_h^++\int_{J+h}e_h^-$ bounds
$\Xi_h^\varepsilon(J)$. Apply \eqref{eq:v90-volume-finite} and
\eqref{eq:v90-uniform-end}. Since $h^{5/8}\le h^{1/32}$ for
$h<1$, the result follows. Negative translations follow by translating
$J$ and interchanging its two arguments. The common segment kernels
fix the same representatives throughout; this is an integral identity
for all shifts, not a supremum over exceptional fiber versions.
\end{proof}

\section{The estimated gain and the remaining upper-source measures}
\label{sec:v93-upper}
The positive-growth budget can be estimated on its entire noncritical
part, uniformly in every previously fixed positive cutoff. This leaves
actual ancestral entrances and critical positive growth, rather than
an integrated oscillation norm, in the pointwise inequality.

For a fixed gradient threshold $\rho>0$, let
$G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,<\rho}$ and
$G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,\ge\rho}$ be the terms in
\eqref{eq:v93-ancestral-budget} restricted at the intermediate roof
to $z<\rho$ and $z\ge\rho$, respectively. Define their sharp versions
by removing the ramp. The cutoff is on the physical intermediate
state, not on an initially transported surrogate source.

\begin{theorem}[Complete noncritical positive gain]
\label{thm:v93-gain}
At every finite count and almost every roof,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-gain-finite}
 G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,\ge\rho,\sharp}(t)
 \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\int_{t-r}^t v^\rho(u)\,du,
\end{equation}
where $v^\rho$ is the actual truncated first-inverse-gradient source
in Input~\ref{input:v93-analytic}. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-gain-ordered}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k,c}m^2
       \|G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,\ge\rho,\sharp}\|_\infty
        \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r.
\end{equation}
The supremum over $c$ ranges over all Borel prefixes at that count.
The leading constant is independent of $\rho$, $r$ and the two
original exceptional-source cutoffs. Each $\rho,r>0$ is fixed before
the collision limit. The theorem does not assert its conclusion at
$\rho=0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Before applying the absolute bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:v93-traces},
keep the physical density in the product rule:
\[
 [(f_\sigma^\varepsilon)'(u)]_+
 \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
                  A_\sigma(u)I_m(\Psi_\sigma(u))/z(\Psi_\sigma(u)).
\]
For each intermediate roof $u$, ancestors of a fixed selected target
form a subfamily of the original exact fiber, counted once by the
Borel segment map. Integrating this density over that subfamily and
then over $u\in(t-r,t)$ is bounded by the right side of
\eqref{eq:v93-gain-finite}. No trace is equated to unweighted flux,
and no factor counting physical words is inserted. Apply the
positive-cutoff estimate \eqref{eq:v93-cutoff-input} with interval
length $r$ to prove \eqref{eq:v93-gain-ordered}. Its finite-count
remainder depends on $\rho$; the legal ordered estimate has one
leading constant for all previously fixed positive $\rho$.
\end{proof}

Combining Theorems~\ref{thm:v93-pointwise} and \ref{thm:v93-gain}
gives the following estimate on the original, unrenormalized source:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-upper-finite}
 R_c^\varepsilon(t)\le
 \frac1r\int_{t-r}^tR_c^\varepsilon(s)\,ds
 +B_{c,r}^\varepsilon(t)+G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,<\rho}(t)
 +C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\int_{t-r}^t v^\rho(u)\,du.
\end{equation}
Every term is formed at finite count. In particular the left side
includes selected points with arbitrarily small initial gradient and
arbitrarily short total residence.

\subsection{A source-specific upper-spike certificate}
For the sharp budgets put
\[
 H_{c,r,\rho}^\varepsilon(t)
 =B_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,\sharp}(t)
       +G_{c,r}^{\varepsilon,<\rho,\sharp}(t).
\]
Fix a roof $t$ and a level $\lambda>0$. If
$m^2R_c^\varepsilon(t)\ge\lambda$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-spike-test}
 m^2H_{c,r,\rho}^\varepsilon(t)
 +Cm^2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\int_{t-r}^t v^\rho\le\lambda/2,
\end{equation}
then \eqref{eq:v93-persistence} proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-spike-width}
 m^2R_c^\varepsilon(s)\ge\lambda/2
            \quad\text{for almost every }s\in(t-r,t).
\end{equation}
This is persistence on an entire prescribed interval, not only a
weak bound for the measure of some superlevel set. It is quantitative
and holds for the original selector, but condition
\eqref{eq:v93-spike-test} is not asserted uniformly at every roof.

For example, if a fixed interval containing $(t-r,t)$ has
$\int m^2R_c^\varepsilon<\lambda r/2$, then an upper spike forces
the left side of \eqref{eq:v93-spike-test} to exceed $\lambda/2$.
Alternatively its critical measurable-set norm must be at least
$(\lambda/2)r^{31/32}$ unless the same physical budget is large.
The already proved source-mass and critical-norm decay therefore
force any surviving high spike into a concentration of actual
ancestral entrance traces or critical positive optical growth.
The noncritical gain has already been paid by
\eqref{eq:v93-gain-ordered}.

\subsection{An upper error estimate in the original topology}
For the full bad source take $c_\sigma=b_\sigma$ and omit $c$.
On the original central target define
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak I_{\varepsilon,M}(r)
   &=\limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2\esssup_{t\in\mathcal C(M)}
                                        B_r^\varepsilon(t),\notag\\
 \mathfrak C_{\varepsilon,M}(r)
   &=\lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
        \esssup_{t\in\mathcal C(M)}G_r^{\varepsilon,<\rho}(t).
                                             \label{eq:v93-forcing-charges}
\end{align}
The latter limit is monotone and extended nonnegative. It is taken
\emph{after} the normalized essential supremum and collision limit.
These positive quantities are not signed cancellations of exits.

\begin{theorem}[The scalar upper half with its positive mechanisms separated]
\label{thm:v93-upper-endpoint}
Under the retained analytic inputs, for all large fixed $B$ and fixed
$r>0$, with $\varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v93-endpoint}
 \mathcal E_M\le C_MB^{-1/192}
       +\mathfrak I_{\varepsilon(B),M}(r)
       +\mathfrak C_{\varepsilon(B),M}(r)
       +C(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})r.
\end{equation}
The first and last terms are estimated. The two positive physical
forcing terms are retained, not asserted to vanish. In particular,
vanishing of their sum along a legal choice $r(B)$ with
$(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})r(B)\to0$ is sufficient for the original
pointwise assertion. Necessity of this additional forcing condition
is not claimed.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Use \eqref{eq:v93-upper-finite} with the original full bad source.
Its backward average is at most $2A_rb^\varepsilon$. Fix
$B,r,\rho$ and every auxiliary band before the collision limit.
The fixed-width estimate gives $C\varepsilon^{1/16}$ for the
normalized average, while Theorem~\ref{thm:v93-gain} bounds the
noncritical gain by $C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r$. Only then let
$\rho\downarrow0$ in the remaining critical term. No integral or
supremum is interchanged with this limit. Finally insert the positive
scalar remainder and use
$\varepsilon(B)^{1/16}=O(B^{-1/192})$.
For example $r(B)=c\varepsilon(B)^2$ makes the explicit last term
vanish, but does not estimate either forcing term. Every such width
is fixed before its collision limit, with $B$ outermost.
\end{proof}

The entrance measure may contain critical directional atoms; the
critical growth may concentrate after the collision normalization.
The uniform per-sheet modulus does not bound the complete transverse
sum. These are precisely the reasons that
\eqref{eq:v93-endpoint} is not yet a charge-zero theorem. It is a
pointwise source comparison, with signed physical losses and artificial
prefix losses accounted for before the upper estimate, rather than
another bounded normalization or finite-roof-norm conclusion.

\section{A quadratic physical cap at the critical gradient}
\label{sec:v98-cap}
The finite-count spectral error in \eqref{eq:v94-critical-finite}
has only a square-root gain in the gradient cutoff. Integrating that
error against the first inverse gradient is not legitimate. We obtain
a second, quadratic bound from the two-dimensional physical map. Its
constant is an explicitly weighted multiplicity, retained throughout
rather than replaced by an unestimated word count.

Fix $0<b_0<1/8$ within the range of \eqref{eq:v94-critical-finite}.
On the regular exact event put $G(x)=R(-p_0(x),p_m(x))$ and $z=|G|$.
The retained endpoint Hessian satisfies
$\lambda_\circ I\le K=D_q^2F\le\Lambda_\circ I$ in endpoint angles
$q=(\alpha_0,\alpha_m)$. The optical normalization is
$\omega=|\partial_{p_0}\alpha_m|^{-1}$.
Define, with physical states counted once,
\begin{align}
 D_{m,R,n,k}(v)
  &=\sum_{x\in\Pi^{\rm reg}:G(x)=v}
       \frac{I_m(x)\omega(x)}{4\pi c_*\det K(x)},\label{eq:v98-gradient-density}\\
 \mathcal K_m
  &=1+\pi\sup_{R,n,k}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{|v|<b_0}
                                      D_{m,R,n,k}(v).
                                      \label{eq:v98-weighted-multiplicity}
\end{align}
These definitions involve neither the roof target nor an inverse
power of $z$. The factor $I_m$ is the full optical insertion from
\eqref{eq:v94-derivative}.

\begin{lemma}[Physical area formula and a finite weighted cap]
\label{lem:v98-quadratic-cap}
For every finite $m$, $\mathcal K_m<\infty$, uniformly over the
permitted radius and exact labels. For $0<b<b_0$ and every interval
$J$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-quadratic-cap}
        \int_J u_b(t)\,dt\le\mathcal K_m b^2.
\end{equation}
More precisely, if $N_m$ bounds the cardinalities of the regular
physical fibers of $G$ at count $m$, and $v_*=2\tau_-/R_+$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-finiteness-bound}
 \mathcal K_m\le1+C N_m(1+v_*)^{-(m-1)}.
\end{equation}
Equation~\eqref{eq:v98-finiteness-bound} establishes finiteness only;
no collision-uniform estimate of its right side is assumed.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
First variation gives $F_{\alpha_0}=-Rp_0$. Change of variables from
$(\alpha_0,p_0)$ to endpoint angles has density $\omega$. The
Jacobian of $q\mapsto G(q)$ is $\det K>0$. Thus the area formula,
applied on injective local pieces and summed without multiplicity of
charts, gives
\[
 G_\#(I_m\bar\nu)=D_{m,R,n,k}(v)\,dv.
\]
Equivalently $|\det D_{(\alpha_0,p_0)}G|=\det K/\omega$.
This identity uses the original collision normalization and counts
physical preimages, not representatives in overlapping charts.
Truncation of $I_m$, followed by monotone convergence, justifies the
formula before its boundedness has been established.

Here is a bound for each summand uniform through internal grazing.
For flight lengths $L_i\ge\tau_-$ the retained positive optical
recursion is
\[
 y_1=L_0,\quad f_0=1,\quad
 f_i=f_{i-1}+\frac{2y_i}{Rc_i},\quad
 y_{i+1}=y_i+L_i f_i,\quad
 \omega=\frac{Rc_0c_m}{y_m}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 y_m\ge\tau_-\prod_{i=1}^{m-1}(1+v_*/c_i).
\]
For a selected internal incidence,
\[
 \frac1{c_i}\prod_j(1+v_*/c_j)^{-1}
 \le v_*^{-1}(1+v_*)^{-(m-2)}.
\]
Since $\sum_iq_0^{d_i}\le2q_0/(1-q_0)$, it follows that
$I_m\omega\le C(1+v_*)^{-(m-1)}$. For one flight the empty
product gives the same conclusion after enlarging $C$.
Division by $\det K\ge\lambda_\circ^2$ bounds each summand.

At a fixed count, the finite-horizon restriction permits only finitely
many lifted scatterer itineraries. The retained finite definable
physical graph, expressed in finitely many circle charts, includes
the first-hit tests, radius parameter and section decisions. The
nonzero Jacobian makes every regular $G$-fiber discrete. Uniform
finiteness for definable families therefore gives a finite $N_m$
\cite{Coste}. Displacement and occupation take finitely many values
at this count. This is used only for fixed-count finiteness and proves
\eqref{eq:v98-finiteness-bound}. Finally discard the roof test on the
upper side, and integrate \eqref{eq:v98-gradient-density} over the
disk $|v|<b$. Its area is $\pi b^2$, proving
\eqref{eq:v98-quadratic-cap}. No change is made to the source being
estimated.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Integration of two different positive caps]
\label{lem:v98-two-caps}
For $E,H,b>0$,
\begin{align}
 &b^{-1}\min(Eb^{1/2},Hb^2)
       +\int_0^b v^{-2}\min(Ev^{1/2},Hv^2)\,dv\notag\\
 &\hspace{25mm}\le3\min\{Hb,E^{2/3}H^{1/3}\}.
                                      \label{eq:v98-two-caps}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The crossing is $v_*=(E/H)^{2/3}$. For $b\le v_*$ the left side
is $2Hb$. For $b>v_*$ it is
$3E^{2/3}H^{1/3}-Eb^{-1/2}$. These formulas prove the claim.
The minimum is a cap on the positive source estimate, not on a
signed spectral remainder considered by itself.
\end{proof}

Define the actual untruncated source
\[
 w_b(t)\,dt=F_\#(I_mz^{-1}\one_{\{0<z<b\}}\bar\nu).
\]
It has a finite, absolutely continuous roof measure at every count.

\begin{theorem}[First inverse gradient with a complete finite-count error]
\label{thm:v98-uncut-insertion}
For one fixed auxiliary band $B_*$, all $m\ge2$, $0<b<b_0$ and
intervals $J$ of length $L$,
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_J w_b
 \le{}&C b^{\alpha-1}(L+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C\min\left\{m^2\mathcal K_m b,\ 
 C_{B_*}^{2/3}(1+B_*L)^{2/3}m^2
              (\mathcal K_m\theta_{B_*}^{2m})^{1/3}\right\}.
                                      \label{eq:v98-uncut-insertion}
\end{align}
The integration goes to gradient zero at finite count. In particular
there is no error proportional to a negative power of a lower cutoff.
The weighted multiplicity $\mathcal K_m$ is not asserted bounded or
subexponential in $m$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $M(v)=m^2\int_Ju_v$. The two positive bounds give
\[
 M(v)\le C(L+B_*^{-1})v^\alpha
   +\min\{Ev^{1/2},Hv^2\},
 \quad E=C_{B_*}(1+B_*L)m^2\theta_{B_*}^m,
 \quad H=m^2\mathcal K_m.
\]
Indeed a nonnegative quantity bounded by both $A+D$ and $V$ is
bounded by $A+\min(D,V)$. Positive layer cake gives exactly
\[
 m^2\int_Jw_b=b^{-1}M(b)+\int_0^b v^{-2}M(v)\,dv.
\]
Apply it first above a positive lower endpoint, and then use monotone
convergence. The leading term is integrable because $\alpha>1$;
its multiplier is $1+(\alpha-1)^{-1}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:v98-two-caps}
integrates the full error. This proves the inequality and finiteness.
Absolute continuity follows from coarea on compact regular roof
charts and exhaustion; the finite critical set has zero source area.
\end{proof}

We isolate the additional estimate which would make this error
negligible. For an unbounded sequence of previously fixed auxiliary
bands, consider the condition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-spectral-capacity}
       m^6\mathcal K_m\theta_{B_*}^{2m}\longrightarrow0.
                         \tag{SC}
\end{equation}
Subexponential growth of $\mathcal K_m$ is sufficient, but is not
proved here. Under \eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity}, first taking the
collision limit and only then the indicated band sequence gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-uncut-limit}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}\sup_{|J|=L}m^2\int_Jw_b
                          \le C Lb^{1/128}.
\end{equation}
Adding $z\ge b_0$ by \eqref{eq:v94-cutoff} gives the bound $CL$
for $v^0=F_\#(I_mz^{-1}\bar\nu)/dt$ at each fixed $L$.
These are implications of the explicit condition, not unconditional
zero-cutoff conclusions. Geometric-pressure results for stable
Jacobian partition sums \cite{BDPressure} concern a different
weighted sum; no identification with \eqref{eq:v98-weighted-multiplicity}
or uniform parameter bound is imported from them.

\section{Two-ended physical traces on the short component}
\label{sec:v98-paired}
For a maximal original segment write
$f_\sigma^\varepsilon(u)=A_\sigma(u)W^\varepsilon(\Psi_\sigma(u))$.
Its nonnegative one-sided traces are denoted by
$f_\sigma^-$ and $f_\sigma^+$. These are the complete physical
traces in \eqref{eq:v94-signed-input}; a critical entrance trace
need not be zero. The comparison below neither pools the occupation
classes nor identifies coincident faces from different incident
components.

Let $H$ be any Borel target restriction supported on
$0<\ell\le\delta$. Define its paired trace source at the original
roof by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-paired-trace}
 T_H^\varepsilon(t)=\int
   \one_{\{a_\sigma<t<b_\sigma\}}\one_H(\Psi_\sigma(t))
                \min\{f_\sigma^-,f_\sigma^+\}\,d\sigma.
\end{equation}
The selector is evaluated at the target in both quantities being
compared. In particular it can be the old low-clock residual, which
need not be a smooth or monotone selector along a segment.

\begin{theorem}[Complete short-source and paired-trace comparison]
\label{thm:v98-paired-trace}
At every finite count and almost every roof,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-paired-finite}
 |R_H^\varepsilon(t)-T_H^\varepsilon(t)|
 \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\int_{t-\delta}^{t+\delta}v^0(u)\,du,
 \qquad v^0\,dt=F_\#(I_mz^{-1}\bar\nu).
\end{equation}
This untruncated positive source is finite at each count by
Theorem~\ref{thm:v98-uncut-insertion} and the bounded-gradient part.
Under \eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-paired-height}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
       \|R_H^\varepsilon-T_H^\varepsilon\|_\infty
                         \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\delta.
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of the Borel target selector. In
particular, the entire selected source on short segments with at
least one grazing endpoint satisfies the same height bound.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Absolute continuity on the closed segment gives, for every interior
$u$ where the representative is defined,
\[
 |f_\sigma^\varepsilon(u)-\min(f_\sigma^-,f_\sigma^+)|
       \le\int_{a_\sigma}^{b_\sigma}|(f_\sigma^\varepsilon)'(v)|\,dv.
\]
Both angular factors and the original guard give
\[
 |(f_\sigma^\varepsilon)'|
 \le C A_\sigma I_m/z+C\varepsilon^{-1}A_\sigma/z
 \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})A_\sigma I_m/z.
\]
Multiply the first inequality by the target selector. All segments
of length at most $\delta$ containing $t$ lie in
$(t-\delta,t+\delta)$. At each intermediate roof the Borel segment
bijection counts their interiors once, so the sum of these positive
integrals is bounded by the displayed integral of $v^0$.
The absolute value of the projected difference is bounded by this
sum of absolute differences. Truncate and exhaust the original
regular source, then use Tonelli. This proves
\eqref{eq:v98-paired-finite} without taking a derivative of the
Borel selector or a trace on its artificial boundary.

Under \eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity}, the complete first inverse
gradient has fixed-width bound $CL$, as proved after
\eqref{eq:v98-uncut-limit}. Apply it at $L=2\delta$.
If an endpoint is grazing, its original weighted trace is zero,
so the minimum in \eqref{eq:v98-paired-trace} is zero. This proves
the final assertion. An incoming critical endpoint with nonzero
trace is not included in that zero-trace argument.
\end{proof}

This comparison does not claim that a minimum commutes with
projection, or that \eqref{eq:v98-paired-trace} is the Jordan positive
part of a signed current. It controls the error of a specific positive
paired-trace comparison by the full physical derivative. The inherited
signed forcing remains formed after projection.

\begin{theorem}[A scalar reduction with distinct geometric obligations]
\label{thm:v98-endpoint}
Choose $q=1/8$, $r=c\varepsilon(B)^4\le r_{\rm col}$,
$a=\sqrt{qr}$ and $\delta=6qr$, with $c>0$ fixed and small.
Use $H=S$ from \eqref{eq:v98-disjoint-residual} in
\eqref{eq:v98-paired-trace}. If
\eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity} holds, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v98-endpoint}
 \mathcal E_M\le\mathcal H_M(T_S^{\varepsilon(B)})
 +C_MB^{-1/192}+C(qr)^{257/256}
                   +C(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})qr.
\end{equation}
Under that same condition, the original pointwise theorem is
equivalent along this schedule to
$\mathcal H_M(T_S^{\varepsilon(B)})\to0$.
Neither \eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity} nor this paired-trace
height decay is asserted established for the full Lorentz family.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The retained finite-count scalar reduction bounds $b^\varepsilon$
by $Y^\varepsilon$ plus the already paid clock and protected
compression terms. Split $Y=C\sqcup S$ before projection.
Theorem~\ref{thm:v98-critical-certificate} pays $C$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:v98-paired-trace} compares $S$ to $T_S$.
The retained positive remainder proves \eqref{eq:v98-endpoint}.
Every scale and auxiliary band is fixed before the collision limit;
\eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity} is invoked only at each such fixed
band. The band sequence is enlarged afterwards, and $B$ is last.

For the schedule, the additional powers are
$(qr)^{257/256}=O(\varepsilon^{257/64})$ and
$(1+\varepsilon^{-1})qr=O(\varepsilon^3)$; both vanish.
Sufficiency follows. Conversely $S^\varepsilon\le b^\varepsilon$,
so scalar closure and the positive remainder imply
$\mathcal H_M(S^{\varepsilon(B)})=O(B^{-1/192})$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:v98-paired-height} then implies decay of $T_S$.
This necessity statement is conditional on the same spectral-capacity
estimate as its sufficiency statement.
\end{proof}

Without \eqref{eq:v98-spectral-capacity}, the finite-count comparisons
\eqref{eq:v98-critical-certificate} and \eqref{eq:v98-paired-finite}
remain valid with the explicit error in
\eqref{eq:v98-uncut-insertion}. Thus the new reduction identifies two
separate tasks: control a weighted two-dimensional momentum-fiber
multiplicity against the spectral error, and control the original
paired positive boundary traces on genuinely short segments. The
first is not a roof-height assumption; the second retains the exact
target selector, physical endpoints and original guard. Finite-count
finiteness does not prove either asymptotic task. Scalar upper closure,
not a finite-norm consequence, still precedes every unrestricted
point-conditioned downstream assertion.

\section{A marked pressure comparison for the actual momentum fibers}
\label{sec:v99-pressure}
Normalize the initial lifted scatterer to the origin. Let
$\mathcal W_j(R)$ be the finite set of realizable physical itineraries
of $j$ flights, retaining the lifted displacement of each step. If
$[w]_R$ is the regular domain of $w$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-word-sum}
 P_j(R)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W_j(R)}
       \sup_{x\in[w]_R\cap M'}J^s_RT_R^j(x),\qquad P_0(R)=1.
\end{equation}
These are geometric upper sums, not replacements for the exact event.
They impose no occupation or section test; those tests are dropped
only on the upper side of the comparison below. There is one fixed
finite step alphabet of size $D$: successive lifted centers are at
distance at most $\tau_++2R_+$. It follows in particular that every
$P_j(R)$ is finite and that each fixed-$j$ supremum over $R$ is finite.

For comparison with the established pressure theory let
$\mathcal Q_j(R)$ be the stable-Jacobian sum at potential parameter
one over the homogeneous continuity partition
$\mathcal M_0^{j,H}$ of \cite[equations (2.4), (2.11)]{BDPressure}.
Its cells retain the true singularities through the terminal time and
homogeneity cuts through time $j-1$. Each cell determines one lifted
physical itinerary. Splitting into those cells can only increase a
sum of suprema of a positive function. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-pressure-domination}
                         P_j(R)\le\mathcal Q_j(R).
\end{equation}
No identification of the two sums is asserted.

Let $\mathcal K_m(R)$ denote \eqref{eq:v98-weighted-multiplicity}
with the radius held fixed. Thus $\mathcal K_m=\sup_R\mathcal K_m(R)$.

\begin{theorem}[Complete momentum-fiber pressure bound]
\label{thm:v99-pressure-comparison}
With a constant depending only on the uniform physical geometry,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-pressure-comparison}
 \mathcal K_m(R)\le 1+C\left[ P_m(R)+D\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}q_0^{d_i}
                       P_i(R)P_{m-i-1}(R)\right].
\end{equation}
All physical preimages, internal incidences and original exact labels
are included. There is no factor counting homogeneity strips at the
marked collision.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix an almost-everywhere momentum target and one exact event. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:v99-unique}, each itinerary supplies at most one
preimage. The denominator in \eqref{eq:v98-gradient-density} is at
least $4\pi c_*\lambda_\circ^2$. The term without a mark is therefore
bounded by $CP_m(R)$ using Lemma~\ref{lem:v99-stable-weight}.

For the mark at $i$, use \eqref{eq:v99-remove-mark}. A full itinerary
is uniquely determined by its first $i$ flights, its single step at
time $i$, and its remaining $m-i-1$ flights, with the last block
translated back to the initial fundamental scatterer. The middle step
has at most $D$ choices. The weighted sum of its possible preimages
is consequently at most $CDP_i(R)P_{m-i-1}(R)$. This argument uses
physical itineraries, not the infinitely many homogeneity strips
whose inverse-incidence weight would no longer be summable after
removing the marked stable factor. Multiplying by $q_0^{d_i}$ and
summing proves the bound after taking the required essential and
exact-label suprema. The finite horizon alphabet and global
uniqueness supply every multiplicity used in this argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded capacity at each fixed radius]
\label{cor:v99-fixed-radius}
For every fixed $R\in I$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-fixed-radius}
                    \sup_{m\ge1}\mathcal K_m(R)<\infty.
\end{equation}
In particular $m^6\mathcal K_m(R)\theta^{2m}\to0$ for every fixed
$0<\theta<1$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For each fixed finite-horizon dispersing table, the pressure theorem
\cite[Lemma 3.8, proof]{BDPressure} gives
$\sup_j\mathcal Q_j(R)<\infty$. Apply
\eqref{eq:v99-pressure-domination} and
\eqref{eq:v99-pressure-comparison}, and use
$\sum_iq_0^{d_i}\le2q_0/(1-q_0)$. This use of the pressure theorem
is now justified by an explicit comparison of the same optical
weight and momentum preimages; it is not a comparison of cardinalities.
\end{proof}

The constant in the cited fixed-table pressure theorem has not been
shown here to be uniform as $R$ varies. The quantifiers in
\eqref{eq:v99-fixed-radius} must not be interchanged. The following
finite-block theorem gives an explicit family-uniform alternative.

\begin{theorem}[Uniform finite-block capacity certificate]
\label{thm:v99-block}
Put $\overline P_j=\sup_{R\in I}P_j(R)$. For every fixed integer
$L\ge1$ define
\[
 \rho_L=\max\{1,\overline P_L^{1/L}\},\qquad
 C_L=\max_{0\le j<L}\overline P_j\rho_L^{-j}.
\]
There is an explicit finite geometric multiple $A_L$ of
$1+C_L+DC_L^2\sum_{i\ge1}2q_0^i$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-block-growth}
                 \mathcal K_m\le A_L\rho_L^m\qquad(m\ge1).
\end{equation}
Consequently (SC) holds at a fixed auxiliary band whenever, for some
fixed $L$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v99-block-certificate}
                 \rho_L\theta_{B_*}^{\,2}<1.\tag{BC}
\end{equation}
If this certificate holds at an unbounded sequence of previously
fixed bands, all radius-uniform consequences of (SC) in the retained
article follow. No numerical verification of (BC) over $I$ is
claimed in this revision.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Splitting a physical itinerary into two consecutive blocks is
injective into the pair of block itineraries. The stable cocycle
gives $P_{j+k}(R)\le P_j(R)P_k(R)$, so also
$\overline P_{j+k}\le\overline P_j\overline P_k$.
Writing $m=vL+j$, $0\le j<L$, proves
$\overline P_m\le C_L\rho_L^m$. Insert this and the corresponding
bound for the two factors in \eqref{eq:v99-pressure-comparison}.
Since $\rho_L\ge1$ and the depth weights are summable, it gives
\eqref{eq:v99-block-growth}. Under (BC),
\[
 m^6\mathcal K_m\theta_{B_*}^{2m}
       \le A_Lm^6(\rho_L\theta_{B_*}^2)^m\longrightarrow0.
\]
All suprema over $R$, block lengths and bands are in the displayed
order. The block is fixed before $m$ and is allowed to depend on the
previously chosen auxiliary band, never on collision count.
\end{proof}

In particular
\[
 \limsup_m m^{-1}\log\mathcal K_m
       \le\inf_{L\ge1}\max\{0,L^{-1}\log\overline P_L\}.
\]
This is an actual uniform growth estimate expressed through geometric
partition sums. It replaces the unquantified fiber cardinality of
module 235. Establishing that its right side is zero, or certifying
the strict inequalities (BC), remains a family-uniform question;
pointwise-in-$R$ pressure bounds alone do not settle it.

\section{Uniform geometric pressure by finitely many transverse tests}
\label{sec:v100-pressure}
The fixed-table conclusion in Corollary~\ref{cor:v99-fixed-radius}
is not interchanged with a supremum over tables. We prove a uniform
bound directly. The argument uses expansion and distortion, but no
mixing time, invariant Cantor rectangle or parameter-dependent
spectral gap.

We use standard collision coordinates $(s,\varphi)$ in this section;
$s$ is physical arclength and $p=\sin\varphi$. Jacobians along curves
refer to Euclidean arclength in these coordinates. The index of a
homogeneity strip is denoted by $k$; its width is $O(|k|^{-3})$.
Let $\mathcal M_0^{m,H}(R)$ be the homogeneous continuity partition
of \cite[(2.4)]{BDPressure}, and set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-Q}
 Q_m(R)=\sum_{A\in\mathcal M_0^{m,H}(R)}
               \sup_{x\in A\cap M_R'}J^sT_R^m(x),\qquad Q_0(R)=1.
\end{equation}
These are geometric partition sums, without the section, guard or
four-record twist. They are used only as positive upper bounds for
the original exact-label fibers through Theorem~\ref{thm:v99-pressure-comparison}.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform geometric constants]\label{lem:v100-geometric}
The given circular family admits one choice of cone bounds,
homogeneity threshold, short-curve length and constants with the
following properties.

For every homogeneous short cone-stable curve $W$, let
$\mathcal G_j(W)$ be its homogeneous inverse-image components,
subdivided at the chosen length scale. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-curve-growth}
 \sum_{V\in\mathcal G_j(W)}\sup_V J_VT_R^j\le C_g,
                                      \qquad j\ge0.
\end{equation}
On one homogeneous backward continuity cell, the ratio of the
inverse Jacobians on any two short cone-stable curves is between
$C_d^{-1}$ and $C_d$, independently of the iterate.

For $A\in\mathcal M_0^{m,H}(R)$, let $B_{m-1}(A)$ be the cell of
$\mathcal M_{-m+1}^{0,H}(R)\vee H$ containing $T_R^{m-1}A$.
There are $\delta_*>0$ and $c_{\rm long}>0$, independent of $R,m$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-long-cell}
 c_{\rm long} Q_m(R)\le
 \sum_{\substack{A\in\mathcal M_0^{m,H}(R)\\
             \operatorname{diam}^u B_{m-1}(A)\ge\delta_*}}
                          \sup_A J^sT_R^m.
\end{equation}
The geometric constant $c_{\rm long}$ is unrelated to the unchanged
section normalization $c_*$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The common geometric bounds are a positive minimum free flight,
a finite maximum free flight, positive lower and upper curvatures,
and bounded third derivatives of the circular boundaries. The
number of possible one-flight lattice displacements is uniformly
finite. Physical arclengths can be identified with fixed collision
circles by uniformly bounded linear changes of coordinate. Thus
\cite[Theorem 2.5 and Remark 2.7]{DZUniform} applies with one set of
geometric constants. Its uniform growth estimate, Lemma 3.2(b), is
\eqref{eq:v100-curve-growth}. The whole-cell distortion statement is
\cite[Lemma 2.2]{BDPressure}; its proof sums the common hyperbolic
contraction and homogeneous distortion bounds and therefore gives
one $C_d$ on this family. It compares different stable curves, not
merely two points on the same curve.

For clarity, the uniformity needed in the long-cell lemma is a
finite geometric choice, rather than a compactness assertion about
$\sup_m Q_m(R)$. Use \cite[Lemmas 3.3, 3.5 and 3.6]{BDPressure}
only at potential parameter one and additional potential zero.
In their proof choose the one-step small-curve contraction
$\vartheta<1$ and its prefactor $C_0$ from the common growth bounds.
Choose an integer $n_1$ so that the resulting geometric loss series
$C_0\sum_{j\ge1}\vartheta^{jn_1}$ is smaller than the fixed loss
fraction used in Lemma 3.5. This choice is independent of $R$.
The short-curve threshold for the first $2n_1$ iterates is then chosen
using the same one-step expansion and homogeneous tail. Only finitely
many iterates have been specified at this stage. Their branchwise
H\"older moduli and complexity bounds are uniform: the free-flight
formula has the same square-root contact singularity, bounded
geometric coefficients and a finite common displacement alphabet.
The identical construction applies to $T_R^{-1}$.

In the proof of Lemma 3.6 choose the smaller of the forward and
backward length thresholds, and then choose $n_2$ with
$C\Lambda^{-n_2}$ below that threshold, where $\Lambda>1$ is the
common cone expansion. Partition a backward cell by its most recent
ancestor having the prescribed unstable length. The branches which
have not yet reached that length are charged to the preceding
small-curve geometric series. Applying distortion and summing that
series leaves a fixed positive fraction of the full pressure on
cells with a long unstable curve. This is precisely the inequality
of that lemma, with its $\delta_2/3$ renamed $\delta_*$. Its remaining
finitely many initial iterates are handled by reducing the common
length threshold: the homogeneous tails have uniformly summable
weights, and the remaining finite physical branches have the same
uniform geometric bounds. This gives \eqref{eq:v100-long-cell}.
No step of this choice uses Proposition 3.14 of that paper, its
mixing argument, or its table-dependent return time. The section normalization is not used in this geometric lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite testing of long backward cells]
\label{lem:v100-tests}
There are integers $N_*,D_*<\infty$ and, for each $R$, homogeneous
short cone-stable curves $W_1(R),\ldots,W_{N_*}(R)$ such that every
cell $B$ in \eqref{eq:v100-long-cell} meets at least one test curve.
The same $N_*$ works for all $R$ and all $m$. At most $D_*$ different
forward cells $A$ have a given $B_{m-1}(A)=B$.

Distinct backward cells assigned to one test can be represented by
distinct members of $\mathcal G_{m-1}(W_j)$. The representatives are
chosen for summation only and introduce no new physical stopping rule.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A homogeneous cone-unstable arc of length $\delta_*$ has a coordinate
projection of length at least $c\delta_*$. Since its slope is bounded
above and away from zero, it cannot lie in a homogeneity strip of
width smaller than $c'\delta_*$. Hence only finitely many strip indices
can occur. Work in finitely many overlapping lifted collision charts.
Choose a slope strictly inside the common stable cone. The affine
coordinate transverse to lines of that slope increases along every
cone-unstable arc at speed bounded below by a positive constant.
A grid of transverse levels with mesh less than $c''\delta_*$ must
therefore meet every such arc in its interior. Split these grid lines
into overlapping short pieces and intersect with the finitely many
relevant homogeneity strips. This produces at most $N_*$ tests.
The overlap removes chart-end ambiguities. A generic translation of
the grids avoids coincidence with true singular arcs; an arbitrarily
small such translation preserves the strict mesh inequality. Tests
are chosen separately for each $R$, with the same numerical bounds;
no radius-independent exceptional null set is required.

The boundary of a backward continuity cell consists of cone-unstable
arcs and horizontal homogeneity boundaries, in lifted collision
coordinates. Such cells are convex along a cone-stable test: successive
crossings of their unstable boundaries separate different cells, and
an arc cannot end freely in a regular interior. This remains true
under inverse iteration, by invariance of the unstable cone and the
fact that new arc ends lie on previous singular or strip boundaries.
Consequently each connected test intersection has one homogeneous
inverse branch. Extra length subdivisions can only refine it; choose
one of them. Different $B$'s give disjoint inverse branches, so no
member is charged twice.

Finally $T_R^{m-1}A$ is obtained from $B$ by the last physical
one-step singularity cuts. There is no homogeneity cut at the final
image in the definition of $\mathcal M_0^{m,H}$. The one-step true
singularity set has a uniformly bounded number of lifted cone-stable
arcs, because only a fixed finite set of disks can be the next hit.
Each such arc crosses a cone-stable-convex backward cell in at most
one connected arc. Their ordered graph cuts make at most $D_*' +1$
components; take $D_*=D_*'+1$. This last bound counts physical
one-step cuts, not the countably many homogeneous strips.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform bounded geometric pressure]
\label{thm:v100-uniform-pressure}
There is $Q_*<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-uniform-pressure}
             \sup_{R\in[R_-,R_+]}\sup_{m\ge0}Q_m(R)\le Q_*.
\end{equation}
In particular the actual geometric itinerary sums $P_m(R)$ in
\eqref{eq:v99-word-sum} satisfy the same bound.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
There is a uniform one-step bound $J^sT_R\le C_1$. For every forward
cell $A$ counted in \eqref{eq:v100-long-cell}, put $B=B_{m-1}(A)$.
Dropping the last stable factor gives
\[
 \sup_AJ^sT_R^m\le
 C_1\sup_{y\in B\cap M_R'}
          J^sT_R^{m-1}(T_R^{-m+1}y).
\]
Assign $B$ to its first meeting test $W_j$. Compare a true stable
curve through $y$ to that test inside the same homogeneous backward
cell, using Lemma~\ref{lem:v100-geometric}. Inverting the two
backward Jacobians bounds the last supremum by
$C_d\sup_V J_VT_R^{m-1}$ for a representing homogeneous inverse
component $V$ of $W_j$. The distortion bound is uniform over the
whole cell; the test need not meet the particular final one-step
subcell $T_R^{m-1}A$.

There are at most $D_*$ such subcells per $B$. The injective
assignment in Lemma~\ref{lem:v100-tests} and the curve growth bound
therefore give, for $m\ge2$,
\[
 c_{\rm long}Q_m(R)
 \le C_1D_*C_d\sum_{j=1}^{N_*}
       \sum_{V\in\mathcal G_{m-1}(W_j)}\sup_VJ_VT_R^{m-1}
 \le C_1D_*C_dN_*C_g.
\]
The same geometric one-step estimates bound $Q_1$ uniformly, and
$Q_0=1$. Taking the larger of these constants proves the assertion.
Finally the homogeneous continuity partition refines each physical
itinerary; positivity gives $P_m(R)\le Q_m(R)$. Every sum is taken
at finite collision count before either supremum. In particular
\eqref{eq:v100-uniform-pressure} is not obtained by interchanging
$\sup_R$ with a fixed-table collision limit.
\end{proof}

\section{Uniform momentum capacity and uncut gradient moments}
\label{sec:v100-capacity}
The preceding pressure theorem applies to the exact optical weight
through the already proved marked comparison. No unweighted word
count or unspecified finite fiber multiplicity enters the conclusion.

\begin{theorem}[Uniform weighted momentum capacity]
\label{thm:v100-capacity}
For the original radius family and every finite collision count,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-capacity}
 \mathcal K_m\le K_*:=
 1+C\left(Q_*+D Q_*^2\frac{2q_0}{1-q_0}\right)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every fixed admissible auxiliary band,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-SC}
       m^6\mathcal K_m\theta_{B_*}^{2m}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
The strict finite-block criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:v99-block}
is also satisfied analytically for a sufficiently large fixed block
at each such band.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Insert $P_j(R)\le Q_*$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:v99-pressure-comparison}.
The complete depth sum is at most $2q_0/(1-q_0)$; its coefficient
$D$ counts the single omitted physical step. Global fixed-itinerary
momentum uniqueness and the optical/stable comparison have already
been proved before this insertion. Thus this bounds the actual
$I_m\omega/\det K$ sum on each momentum fiber, including all
internal incidence scales and all exact labels.

Since $\theta_{B_*}<1$, the right side of
$m^6\mathcal K_m\theta_{B_*}^{2m}\le K_*m^6\theta_{B_*}^{2m}$
tends to zero with $B_*$ fixed. Also
$\sup_R P_L(R)\le Q_*$, so that
\[
 \max\{1,(\sup_R P_L(R))^{1/L}\}\theta_{B_*}^2<1
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 L>\frac{\log\max(1,Q_*)}{-2\log\theta_{B_*}}.
\]
This is an existence certificate with finite constants, not a
numerical interval computation of an optimal block or mixing rate.
The block may depend on the already fixed auxiliary band, never on
$m$. Equation~\eqref{eq:v100-SC} itself does not require a block
choice at all.
\end{proof}

Put $\alpha=129/128$. For $1\le p<\alpha$ and $0<b<b_0$, define
an actual nonnegative measure on the same exact event by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-moment-source}
 w_{p,b}(t)\,dt
   =F_\#\!\left(I_m z^{-p}\one_{\{0<z<b\}}\bar\nu\right).
\end{equation}
Here the exponent acts on $z$, not on $I_m$; no assertion about
$(I_m/z)^p$ is made. Values on the original area-null critical set
are immaterial. The source is untruncated at $z=0$.

\begin{lemma}[The two-cap moment integral]\label{lem:v100-layer}
If $E,H,b>0$ and $1/2<p<2$, then
\begin{align}
 &b^{-p}\min\{E b^{1/2},H b^2\}
   +p\int_0^b v^{-p-1}\min\{E v^{1/2},H v^2\}\,dv\notag\\
 &\qquad\le C_p\min\{H b^{2-p},
                 E^{(4-2p)/3}H^{(2p-1)/3}\}.
                                                   \label{eq:v100-layer}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The quadratic cap alone gives $2H b^{2-p}/(2-p)$.
The caps agree at $v_0=(E/H)^{2/3}$. Below $v_0$ use $Hv^2$;
above it use $Ev^{1/2}$. The two resulting integrals are bounded by
multiples of $Hv_0^{2-p}$ and $Ev_0^{1/2-p}$, respectively, and
both equal $E^{(4-2p)/3}H^{(2p-1)/3}$. The boundary term has the
same bound. Finiteness at zero uses $p<2$, and at the extended
upper limit it uses $p>1/2$. Both inequalities hold together,
proving their minimum after increasing $C_p$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform uncut first and nearby gradient moments]
\label{thm:v100-uncut}
For every $1\le p<\alpha$, every fixed auxiliary band $B_*$ and
$|J|=L$, the source in \eqref{eq:v100-moment-source} satisfies
\begin{align}
 m^2\int_J w_{p,b}\le{}&C_p b^{\alpha-p}(L+B_*^{-1})\notag\\
 &+C_p\min\left\{m^2K_*b^{2-p},
 [C_{B_*}(1+B_*L)]^{(4-2p)/3}
 m^2K_*^{(2p-1)/3}\theta_{B_*}^{m(4-2p)/3}\right\}.
                                               \label{eq:v100-uncut-finite}
\end{align}
Constants are uniform in radius, exact labels, collision count and
interval location. In particular, for each fixed $b,L>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-uncut-limit}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}\sup_{|J|=L}m^2\int_J w_{p,b}
                                      \le C_p Lb^{\alpha-p}.
\end{equation}
The full source $v^0=F_\#(I_m/z\,\bar\nu)/dt$ obeys
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-v0}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}\sup_{|J|=L}m^2\int_Jv^0\le CL.
\end{equation}
No spectral-capacity hypothesis remains in these conclusions.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The endpoint-momentum area formula and
Theorem~\ref{thm:v100-capacity} give
$\int_Ju_v\le K_*v^2$, at every count and every $v>0$ in range.
The inherited critical-volume estimate gives
\[
 m^2\int_Ju_v\le C v^\alpha(L+B_*^{-1})+Ev^{1/2},
 \qquad E=C_{B_*}(1+B_*L)m^2\theta_{B_*}^m.
\]
The source on the left is nonnegative. Combining its two upper
bounds therefore retains the leading term and caps the error by
$\min(Ev^{1/2},Hv^2)$, with $H=m^2K_*$.

Apply the positive identity
\[
 z^{-p}\one_{\{z<b\}}=
 b^{-p}\one_{\{z<b\}}+
 p\int_0^b v^{-p-1}\one_{\{z<v\}}\,dv.
\]
Integrate first from a positive lower endpoint and then use monotone
convergence. The leading integral is finite because $p<\alpha$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:v100-layer} pays the entire error down to zero.
The exponents of $m^2$ in the two factors sum to one, giving
\eqref{eq:v100-uncut-finite}. The physical quadratic bound also
proves finiteness of the measure at each count. Local coarea away
from its area-null critical set, followed by monotone exhaustion,
gives its density.

Fix $b,L,B_*$ before the collision limit. The second expression in
the minimum tends to zero uniformly in $R,n,k$. Enlarge $B_*$ only
afterwards to obtain \eqref{eq:v100-uncut-limit}. For $p=1$, add
the region $z\ge b_0/2$ using the inherited complete $I_m$ source
bound. This proves \eqref{eq:v100-v0}. Neither a collision-dependent
cutoff nor a band growing with $m$ is used.
\end{proof}

\section{Uniform critical recovery and the positive short trace}
\label{sec:v100-recovery}
The capacity obstruction and the positive short-trace obstruction
are different. The former has now been discharged uniformly in the
radius. We record exactly which essential-height conclusions this
supplies, and keep the latter source explicit.

Use the original residual partition from Section~\ref{sec:v98-critical}:
$d=2qr$, $\mathsf S=Y\cap\{\ell\le3d\}$ and
$\mathsf C=Y\cap\{\ell>3d\}$. For a Borel target selector $H$
supported on segments of total length at most $\delta$, write
$R_H^\varepsilon$ for its original weighted source and
$T_H^\varepsilon$ for the same-segment minimum of the two weighted
physical endpoint traces. No selector trace is introduced.

\begin{theorem}[Radius-uniform recovery without a capacity premise]
\label{thm:v100-recovery}
For the entire prescribed radius interval, the critical target source
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-critical-height}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2\|\mathsf C^\varepsilon\|_\infty
          \le C d(a^2+2\Lambda_\circ d)^{1/256}.
\end{equation}
Every previously fixed Borel selection on short segments satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:v100-paired-height}
 \limsup_m\sup_{R,n,k}m^2
       \|R_H^\varepsilon-T_H^\varepsilon\|_\infty
                         \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})\delta.
\end{equation}
In particular this bounds the complete selected source on all
segments with an actual grazing endpoint, since their paired minimum
is zero. Neither estimate requires a positive initial-gradient or
internal-incidence cutoff. The supremum is over the original exact
labels, not a neighboring-label enlargement.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The finite-count target certificate in
Theorem~\ref{thm:v98-critical-certificate} reads
\[
 \mathsf C^\varepsilon(t)\le
 C_0\int_t^{t+d}w_{1,b}(u)\,du,
 \qquad b=(a^2+2\Lambda_\circ d)^{1/2}.
\]
Its low-clock argument forces a loss of at least one half of the
initial angular density inside a full surviving forward interval.
The target-direction map is injective at each intermediate roof.
Apply \eqref{eq:v100-uncut-limit} with interval length $d$;
$b^{1/128}=(a^2+2\Lambda_\circ d)^{1/256}$ gives
\eqref{eq:v100-critical-height}.

For the other assertion the inherited same-segment trace comparison
is already a finite-count inequality on common kernels:
\[
 |R_H^\varepsilon(t)-T_H^\varepsilon(t)|
 \le C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})
              \int_{t-\delta}^{t+\delta}v^0(u)\,du.
\]
The target selector is held at $t$ and not differentiated. The Borel
segment bijection supplies multiplicity one for all joining intervals.
Equation~\eqref{eq:v100-v0} now pays the right side uniformly in the
radius, proving \eqref{eq:v100-paired-height}. A grazing endpoint has
zero original optical trace. A backward critical endpoint need not,
and is not discarded by this statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The original uniform pointwise reduction]
\label{thm:v100-endpoint}
Keep $q=1/8$, $\varepsilon(B)=A_0B^{-1/12}$,
$r=c\varepsilon(B)^4$, $a=\sqrt{qr}$ and $\delta=6qr$.
For all sufficiently large fixed $B$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal E_M\le{}&\mathcal H_M(T_{\mathsf S}^{\varepsilon(B)})
       +C_MB^{-1/192}
       +C(qr)^{257/256}
       +C(1+\varepsilon(B)^{-1})qr.
                                               \label{eq:v100-endpoint}
\end{align}
Unlike the earlier family-wide reduction, this assertion has no
additional condition (SC) or finite-block margin as a hypothesis.
It uses the inherited physical and four-record analytic inputs and
the uniform pressure theorem proved above.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The running-compression reduction is an identity and upper comparison
on the original source before its roof supremum. Its residual is the
disjoint sum $\mathsf C^\varepsilon+\mathsf S^\varepsilon$.
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:v100-recovery} to each part and the retained
positive scalar remainder. With $a^2=qr$ and $d=2qr$, the critical
cost in \eqref{eq:v100-critical-height} is $C(qr)^{257/256}$.
The paired comparison cost is $C(1+\varepsilon^{-1})qr$.
All auxiliary bands are fixed before the collision limit and enlarged
afterwards. The common uniform constants permit the radius supremum
inside that limit; no fixed-radius conclusion is used in its place.
This gives \eqref{eq:v100-endpoint}.

Under the retained outer schedule the explicit costs have sizes
$B^{-1/192}$, $O(\varepsilon^{257/64})$ and $O(\varepsilon^3)$.
They tend to zero with $B$ last. Thus decay of the positive paired
height along this schedule suffices to finish the original uniform
upper half, and hence the full pointwise theorem with the retained
lower half. That paired-height decay is not proved here.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The remaining positive source]\label{rem:v100-positive}
The minimum in $T_{\mathsf S}^\varepsilon$ is taken before the
physical sheets are summed. It is not the Jordan positive part of
an already projected signed current. A small difference between the
two traces cannot bound their positive minimum. On nongrazing short
segments both traces may be positive, including at a backward
critical entrance. Theorems~\ref{thm:v100-capacity} and
\ref{thm:v100-recovery} remove the separate family-uniform capacity
premise; they do not supply a boundary deconcentration theorem for
this positive minimum. Accordingly the unrestricted upper pointwise
law, full raw local limit and unrestricted point-conditioned
consequences are not marked proved. The original target, all zero
arithmetic classes and the scalar-first normalization order remain
unchanged.
\end{remark}

\section{A transverse coordinate for the positive paired source}
\label{sec:v102-pair-coarea}
Fix the collision count, radius and exact label. A maximal segment of
